design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (cargo_claims_desk, claims category, workflow task). Frozen 2026-09-14 10:05:00 CEST.

[1 Why this is a good test] The caller asks for one thing: to have the thawed cartons in reefer container AHLU5412312 added to the claim running on the shipment and to know today whether the line pays for them (round 2 wording; she never asks to lodge). The scored writes are three policy-computed values plus two closures: (a) the settlement of a DIFFERENT, already-documented claim (container AHLU5412230) that the caller never mentions, 22704.00; (b) the notice amount the line puts on the new notice, 103200.00; (c) the controlled rejection reason of the new notice, notice_out_of_time. The agent must discover from the published rules that the loss cannot be added to an existing file and needs a notice of its own ('Each notice names one container and one loss; a loss found in another container of the same shipment is never added to a claim file already on the cover and needs a notice of its own.'), that a notice is decided only once registered, and from claims_ext_notice_container_value ('A further notice can be lodged on a cover only when no claim is open on it: a claim still open on the cover whose documents are complete is decided by the desk before the further notice is lodged.') that the cover's open claim blocks the request, decide that claim by settlement (reconciling claim files, the waybill's declared value, tier parameters and the 12-month approvals on the cover), close it, hand the lodging to the caller at the policy notice value, and then decide the registered notice on grounds that turn on dates, the tier and the reefer service of the claimed container. Difficulty comes from reading policy, querying the world and calculating; every tool is a plain CRUD write.

[2 Scope snapshot] Occupied before this task: nothing (task 0). Claimed here: claims_ext_settlement_invoice_share (approve_claim_settlement_060ed8c3), claims_ext_notice_container_value (lodge_cargo_claim_268664bf, user), claims_ext_lodging_rejection_grounds (reject_cargo_claim_5f9631bd), workflow claims_wf_further_notice_on_open_cover, and close_cargo_claim_a3572c28 as the workflow's non-computing closure step. Left for task 1 (independent, load-bearing): the pre-departure side of the product - binding a quoted cover (claims_cover_bound), charging its premium (claims_premium_charged, contract-rank discount) and the cover holder's own premium remittance (claims_premium_paid) - none of which this task touches. The single workflow is claimed here, so task 1 is a non-workflow task.

[3 Policies, lineage, triggers, overrides] claims_ext_settlement_invoice_share: subject claims_settlement_approved, base_policy_refs = claims_agg_annual_aggregate, claims_coverage_and_exclusions, claims_settlement_calculation (every base policy on that subject), trigger state_due (a documented open claim is owed a decision whoever calls). Overrides, declared in overwrite: (i) claims_settlement_calculation 'Under hague_visby_limitation the line pays the proven loss, the claimed_amount_usd once documents are complete' -> 'The proven loss is the claimed_amount_usd, but never more than the commercial invoice value of the affected packages' (new factor from the transport document, a base asset); (ii) claims_agg_annual_aggregate's holder-wide trailing-365-day aggregate -> the aggregate still available on the same cover over the last 12 whole calendar months; (iii, round 2) its headline 'CargoCare products carry an annual aggregate per cover holder.' -> 'The annual aggregate is kept per cover, not per cover holder, and settlements approved on the holder's other covers of the product do not reduce it.' Everything else of base (Hague-Visby limit, declared value share, uplift, single higher deductible, per-container cap, never negative, desk authority, liability_basis recording) is inherited and restated with the order pinned: uplift acts on the proven loss, the one deductible acts on the uplifted loss basis, the cap acts after the deductible, the aggregate acts last, only the final figure (plus the three named sub-figures) is rounded. claims_ext_notice_container_value: subject claims_claim_lodged, refs claims_notice_and_time_bar, trigger on_request, overwrite [] (base never fixes the amount on a notice). claims_ext_lodging_rejection_grounds: subject claims_claim_rejected, refs claims_coverage_and_exclusions, claims_notice_and_time_bar, trigger state_due, overwrite [] (base lists the reasons; this policy pins their precedence: below_minimum_claim, not_covered_by_tier, claim_time_barred, notice_out_of_time, before the excursion / misdeclaration / peril / documents reasons). Cross-category numeric reads: bol declared_cargo_value_usd and package_count (settlement, notice), booking container_count (notice), reefer variant_name -> rank (rejection); each is exercised by a seeded row of this customer.

[4 Forward and reverse basis sweep] Every world-reading or choosing binding in each compute quotes its rule sentence in compute_basis (e.g. invoice_share <- 'divided by that document's package_count and multiplied by the affected_package_count, rounded to the cent; when that transport document carries no declared cargo value, the proven loss is the claimed_amount_usd'; approved_12m <- 'whose approval date lies fewer than 12 whole calendar months before the approval date' = within_months=12; within_bar <- the same-day / last-day-of-month sentence; within_window <- 'a notice dated on that last day is in time' = DAYS(...) <= window_days). Reverse: every load-bearing rule sentence is claimed - the Hague-Visby and declared-value branches (hv_limit, dv_share, pre_aggregate), the deductible choice (kind_deductible, deductible), the cap moment (cargocare_amount after the deductible), the aggregate (approved_12m, aggregate_left, result), the fallback notice value (container_value else-branch), the cap on a notice (capped_value), the four ground tests and their order (result). The liability_basis recording sentence governs the enum argument, not a compute binding.

[5 Base-invariant card] Step approve (claims_settlement_approved): open_and_documented - cover ed9e8fb4-...status = claim_open and the AHLU5412230 file outcome = documents_complete (system records, pre-action); approved_once - no claims_ledger row carries claim 6d48f2e5-... (A1/A2 approvals and the R1 rejection belong to other files); reefer_rank_for_temperature - reefer service 3d111de7-... on booking e7dc7167-... container AHLU5412230 is AHL Reefer Monitored, rank 2 >= Total's 1; within_desk_authority - 22704.00 <= 50000.00; claims_agg_annual_aggregate has no gate (policy_scope). Step close: claims_settlement_payment has no gate on claims_claim_closed (policy_scope). Step lodge (claims_claim_lodged): claimant_entitled - the claimant is the cover holder Havbris Seafood Export AS (cargo_covers.customer_id = the caller), so the consignee-name test (printed consignee 'Lingang Polar Cold Chain Trading Co., Ltd.') is not needed; claim_cap - non-withdrawn files A1, A2, R1, AHLU5412230 = 4 < 5 (Total), and after steps 9/11 no claim is open. Step reject (claims_claim_rejected): notice_window time gate - anchor cargo_covers.delivery_date 2026-07-30, duration variants.notice_days_non_apparent_damage 30 calendar days, last in-time day 2026-08-29 inclusive; boundary cases: notice 2026-08-29 in time, 2026-08-30 late; the notice 2026-09-14 is late, which is the rejection ground itself; time_bar - 24 months, bar 2028-07-30 inclusive, 2028-07-31 barred; documents_deadline - notice 2026-09-14 + 120 days = 2027-01-12, a documents rejection possible only from 2027-01-13 (exclusive), not the reason used; reject_open_claim - cover claim_open after the lodging (prior step 13); decided_once - no ledger row for ccl_6c9158c0b2c9. The anchors and counting rules are the base temporal_basis copied verbatim into temporal_feasibility.

[6 Business-object card] Target of the settlement: claim 6d48f2e5-604b-433b-8e70-9b61f12a0d74 (container AHLU5412230, 240 cartons, 4800.0 kg, temperature damage, notice 2026-08-14) - the only documents_complete file, correlated by claim_id and cover_id. Included in the aggregate: approvals 9da55da4-... (3784.00, 2026-08-11) and 0a365071-... (6622.00, 2026-08-20) on the same cover; excluded: the paid rows (they settle those approvals, reference_event_id), the premium rows, the R1 rejection (0.00). Target of the notice and rejection: container AHLU5412312 (reefer service 86939aa8-..., AHL Reefer Standard). The earlier withdrawn shortage file cc3e611f-... on the same container is excluded from the claim count and is not the decided notice (outcome withdrawn, earlier notice date).

[7 Problem-tree card] Root: claims_ext_lodging_rejection_grounds (what happens to the claim the caller asks about). Edge 1 (value_input, gate notice_amount): root <- claims_ext_notice_container_value, condition 'The notice being decided is registered on the cover, carrying its amount, container, kind of loss, apparent-at-delivery flag and notice date.', policy_source 'A notice can be decided here only once it has been registered on the cover.', resolved_by lodge_cargo_claim_268664bf; false at frozen_time because no notice_registered file exists (outcomes approved, approved, rejected, withdrawn, documents_complete). Edge 2 (state_gate, gate claims_notice_and_time_bar.claim_cap): notice <- claims_ext_settlement_invoice_share, policy_source 'A further notice can be lodged on a cover only when no claim is open on it: a claim still open on the cover whose documents are complete is decided by the desk before the further notice is lodged.', resolved_by approve_claim_settlement_060ed8c3; false at frozen_time because cargo_covers.status = claim_open and the AHLU5412230 file is documents_complete. Topological order: settlement -> (closure) -> notice -> rejection -> (closure); a chain, so no parallel ambiguity. Deletion sensitivity (verify.py output): skip step 13 -> the rejection recomputes below_minimum_claim instead of notice_out_of_time and claim file ccl_6c9158c0b2c9 is missing; skip step 9 -> notice and reason unchanged but the approval row, the approved outcome and settlement_payable 22704.00 are missing (terminal hash differs). user_scenario never asks to lodge and never names the AHLU5412230 claim's documents, a settlement, the notice amount or any ground (since round 3 it no longer states any assumption about a running claim); tools check no prerequisite (lodge writes over any cover status, reject/approve/close read no status).

[8 World rows and why each exists] customers (1): the caller's profile, credentials +4755527390 / AHL-NO-541208, credit_approved (no premium blocker). bookings (1): AHLU26BGO527604, 4 x 40RH, closed, departed 2026-06-22; container_count 4 is the notice divisor - remove it and the notice falls back to 454080.00/4 = 113520.00. bills_of_lading (1): waybill AHLU2605518342, declared value 412800.00, 4800 cartons, released 2026-07-30; it caps the proven loss at 20640.00 (remove it and the settlement becomes 103200.00 x 1.10 = 113520.00) and fixes the notice at 103200.00. reefer_services (4): one per container; the AHLU5412312 service is AHL Reefer Standard (rank 1) - it keeps temperature damage covered under Total (min rank 1) while being the trap that a reader applying a higher tier's threshold would reject as not_covered_by_tier; without the row the rank is 0 and the reason would flip to not_covered_by_tier. cargo_covers (1): AHL CargoCare Total, claim_open, delivery 2026-07-30, premium clear, settlement_payable 0.00 consistent with the ledger. cargo_claims (5): A1/A2 approved (history the settlement rule reproduces: 40 and 70 cartons x 86.00 x 1.10 = 3784.00 and 6622.00), R1 rejected (excluded peril), W1 withdrawn (excluded from the cap), and the open documents_complete AHLU5412230 file; all carry the notice amount 103200.00 the notice policy fixes, so history teaches the charter. claims_ledger (7): premium charged/paid 1748.21 (454080.00 x 0.35% x 1.10), two approvals and their payments (the 12-month aggregate 10406.00), the R1 rejection. No automatic clause fires: the cover cannot expire while a claim is open; the time bar is 2028-07-30. No stale cache is used (settlement_payable and premium_due equal the ledger).

[9 Persona design] (round 2) Ingrid Solheim-Aas: short, exact, tired; volunteers only the goal in a layperson's terms - the thawed cartons in container AHLU5412312 'added to your claim on this shipment' and an answer today on whether the line pays -. She never asks to lodge a notice. On request: phone, then customer code, then tax number or email; 36 cartons, 720 kilograms, thawed and refrozen, nothing seen at delivery on 30 July; she cannot state a notice value and defers to the line's rule. Passive reactions, each firing only after the agent says so: if told the loss needs a notice of its own, she wants it put in today in any case and submits it herself when handed the tool; if told something else on the shipment must be decided or closed first, she says go ahead; she notes an approval amount without dispute; on a rejection she asks once for the reason, accepts, ends; if told it waits for documents, she will send them and ends. Her last reaction answers the last gold action and asks for nothing more. She never states policy, amounts, grounds or ordering.

[10 Zero-wait causal card] Step 0 approve: cover claim_open, file documents_complete, figures, waybill value (all initial_state_preexisting). Step 1 close: decision = approval row of step 0 (prior_synchronous_tool_effect). Step 2 lodge (owner user, genuinely the claimant's act): cover claim_closed from step 1 (prior_synchronous_tool_effect) + the caller's container, cartons, weight, kind, not-apparent flag (current_user_input). Step 3 reject: registered notice from step 2 (prior_synchronous_tool_effect), delivery date (initial_state_preexisting), frozen_time; the ground is date arithmetic, so no document or survey is awaited. Step 4 close: decision = rejection row of step 3. No survey, payment, document or passage of time is a precondition anywhere; the survey of the AHLU5412230 claim was recorded before the call (documents_complete).

[11 Where a careless agent goes wrong] Lodging over the open claim without deciding it (edge 2); settling at the claimed 103200.00 x 1.10 = 113520.00 instead of capping at the waybill invoice value 20640.00; applying a deductible (Total has none) or the Plus/Premium temperature deductibles; forgetting the 10% uplift (20640.00); using the insured value share (identical 22704.00 here only because insured = CIF x 1.1, but that is the declared_value branch and not the basis); recording liability_basis cover_limit; putting the caller's cartons x 86.00 = 3096.00 on the notice instead of the container value 103200.00; rejecting the notice as not_covered_by_tier by reading the reefer Standard tier against Plus's rank 2; counting 30 days from the notice rather than from delivery; leaving the new notice open for documents although the date ground already applies; skipping either closure.

[12 Standard solution] find_customers(+4755527390) -> verify_customer_identity(phone, customer code) -> find_bookings(AHLU26BGO527604) -> find_cargo_covers(booking) -> find_cargo_claims(cover) -> find_claims_ledger(cover) -> find_bills_of_lading(booking) -> find_reefer_services(booking) -> approve_claim_settlement_060ed8c3(cover, claim 6d48f2e5-..., booking, AHLU5412230, 22704.00, proven_loss) -> close_cargo_claim_a3572c28(cover) -> [caller] lodge_cargo_claim_268664bf(cover, customer, AHLU5412312, temperature_damage, false, 103200.00, 36, 720.0) -> reject_cargo_claim_5f9631bd(cover, ccl_6c9158c0b2c9, notice_out_of_time) -> close_cargo_claim_a3572c28(cover). Workflow closure: steps (tool, owner) = approve/agent, close/agent, lodge/user, reject/agent, close/agent; set(computed_by) = set(computations.policy_id) = set(charter_scope.extended_policies) = the three policies; required_documents in the same order.

[13 Verification actually executed] Script verify.py 0 (verify.py was a temporary authoring script, removed after use; the same handling-time recompute and value_input skip test are re-runnable with: .venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py env/global_container_shipping_line/tasks/cargo_claims_desk --task N) (replays gold with the real share and task tools, evaluates each compute with check_compute.build_env/eval_compute on the handling-time world, then skips each edge's resolving write): 'RECOMPUTE claims_ext_settlement_invoice_share step 9 -> 22704.0 | expected 22704.0 | touched 7'; 'RECOMPUTE claims_ext_notice_container_value step 13 -> 103200.0 | expected 103200.0'; 'RECOMPUTE claims_ext_lodging_rejection_grounds step 15 -> notice_out_of_time | touched 6'; 'SKIP ...rejection_grounds <- ...notice_container_value skipped [13] | rejection -> below_minimum_claim | terminal hash differs: True'; 'SKIP ...notice_container_value <- ...settlement_invoice_share skipped [9] | notice 103200.0, rejection notice_out_of_time | terminal hash differs: True'. Gate commands run (all green): check_extended --task 0 (EXTENDED OK), check_task_tools --task 0 (TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK), replay_tasks --task 0 (REPLAY OK, closure 20 = init 20), check_solvability --task 0 (SOLVABILITY OK, 15 base gates), check_compute --task 0 (COMPUTE OK: 3 comps, 39 factors, 13 history rows, 35 branches), check_grounding --task 0 (GROUNDING OK), check_cross_fire --task 0 (SCOPE OK), check_cache_diff (info only).

[14 Solvability vs GT, and a visible-context draft recompute] Each call's base_preconditions cite pre-action rows correlated by cover_id / claim_id / booking_id+container_number, or the producing prior step (dataflow 2->3 state_effect on cargo_covers.status establishes reject_open_claim). Draft recompute from what a rollout sees (policy prose, tool schemas, finder returns, the caller's lines), with compute/expected masked: the lodge rule says an open documented claim is decided first -> the AHLU5412230 file has no ground (covered temperature damage, rank 2, notice day 15 of 30, within authority) -> approve: proven = min(103200.00, 412800/4800 x 240 = 20640.00) = 20640.00, x1.10 = 22704.00, no deductible, cap and aggregate far away, basis proven_loss -> close -> caller lodges at 412800/4 = 103200.00 -> grounds in order: 103200 >= 50; temperature covered, Standard rank 1 >= 1; 1 month < 24; 46 days > 30 -> notice_out_of_time -> close. Same objects, order and values as gold; no second reading found.

[15 Manual values gates] Long: request -> notice rule -> open-claim gate -> settlement (invoice share, uplift, deductible, cap, aggregate) -> lodging -> ground order -> closure. Broad: tier parameters, 12-month ledger, waybill, booking, reefer tier, dates. Owner=user step is the claimant's own notice. Request boundary: an answer today on the container AHLU5412312 loss, agent may act on the account, the claimant submits any notice herself. Chronology: every volunteered fact (booking, container, 13 September discovery, 30 July delivery) is in initial_state; nothing she says foresees a write. Authority: documents_complete, approvals and statuses come from records only. Revision log: (r1) claims_ledger/booking empty FKs '' -> null and the unread reefer_ledger rows dropped (replay closure); (r2) the helper _money in task_tools.py was counted as a tool -> inlined; (r3) solvability required every gate's action binding as a tool argument -> approve tool gained booking_id and container_number (reefer_rank_for_temperature correlation), gold, tracing and docstring updated and all gates re-run; (r4) workflow scenario narrowed to notices that fail a registration-time ground.

[Round 2 rework - audit policy_task/cargo_claims_desk] F-T0-1 (SOURCE-CHAIN RED): the persona no longer names the lodging. She asks for the loss to be 'added to your claim on this shipment' and for an answer today; the need for a separate notice now comes from the new E2 sentence 'Each notice names one container and one loss; a loss found in another container of the same shipment is never added to a claim file already on the cover and needs a notice of its own.', and the root decision's dependence on a registered notice from E3 'A notice can be decided here only once it has been registered on the cover.' Both prerequisites (E2 value_input, E1 state_gate) are therefore conveyed by policy text; request_alignment, gold_actions[13] intent/discriminator, required_user_inputs and no_user_hint rewritten; lodge necessity updated; the workflow scenario now reads 'A claimant reports a further loss ... needs a notice of its own'. O-T0-2: 'even if it turns out to be small or late' removed. F-2: E2 now registers a notice only when the lodging conditions of claims_notice_and_time_bar hold (claimant admitted, below max_claims_per_cover, no claim open) and states that a claim still awaiting documents keeps the cover closed to further notices; in this world all hold for the fifth claim (4 non-withdrawn < 5). F-3: overwrite now also names 'CargoCare products carry an annual aggregate per cover holder.' and the rule says the aggregate is kept per cover; the holder has one cover here. F-6: E3's zero-day apparent branch is now the delivery-receipt notation (never notice_out_of_time), compute within_window gained that branch; this notice is not apparent, so nothing moves. O-1: E1/E2/E3 read the waybill, booking and reefer service 'recorded for the cover holder' and E2 names the fallback when the booking count is missing (O-14). O-4: 'of which a cover carries at most one'. O-7: approve tool enum gloss for proven_loss now matches E1. O-11/O-T0-5: E2 says the notice amount 'is not the proven loss, which is fixed only when the claim is settled'; the schema gloss itself is frozen blueprint. O-2/O-3: unchanged (Total deductibles are 0.00; delay loss is scoped out by the rule) - retained as observations. O-9: kept (resolved_by must be the depended-on problem's own action; the close is the W step 1 lifecycle transition). O-12/O-T0-3: a lodge -> reject claim_id dataflow cannot be declared because check_extended requires source_table to equal the producer step's base event target (cargo_covers for claims_claim_lodged); the claim_id reaches the reject through the lodge receipt (shared runtime output), and the cover-status state effect 2 -> 3 is declared. O-T0-4: the first close stays - base 'A decided claim closes the open claim on the cover' and the lifecycle lodging edge claim_closed -> claim_open require it; it is scored through the action order. Re-run after the rework: verify (private scratch script) RECOMPUTE 22704.0 / 103200.0 / notice_out_of_time unchanged; SKIP lodge -> below_minimum_claim; SKIP approve -> terminal differs; full gate block green.

[Round 3 rework - audit revision_2] R2-O-T0-1: removed the persona sentence 'You assume the shipment already has a claim running with the line's claims people and that this can simply go with it.'; the request line 'added to your claim on this shipment' is kept because it is the caller's layperson framing of the goal and the request evidence. R2-O1: the approve tool's aggregate_limit gloss now reads 'the annual aggregate still available on the cover reduced the amount', matching E1's per-cover aggregate. O-2, O-3, O-9, O-12/O-T0-3, O-13, O-T0-4 kept as recorded in round 2. Values unchanged (22704.00, 103200.00, notice_out_of_time).

[Round 4 rework - traceability] check_traceability flagged the rejection's claim_id ccl_6c9158c0b2c9: it is minted by the claimant's own (owner=user) lodging call, and a user-owned tool's return reaches the agent only when the simulator relays it. The base eligibility of claims_claim_rejected binds claim_id as an action argument (documents_deadline, decided_once), so the id cannot be removed from the rejection call, and no policy value moved into a tool. Fix at the source: the persona now states that she knows no claim reference before submitting, and that once submitted, her confirmation shows ccl_6c9158c0b2c9, which she reads out straight away, exactly as shown. The value is the lodge tool's deterministic return for exactly the gold arguments (cover, customer, AHLU5412312, temperature_damage, false, 103200.00, 36, 720.0). The step-15 tracing and required_user_inputs now cite that line. Persona, tree and values are otherwise unchanged; no prerequisite is named (the line fires only after the lodging the agent itself hands over).
user_scenario: You are Ingrid Solheim-Aas, who coordinates logistics and cargo claims for Havbris Seafood Export AS in Bergen. You are calm, exact and a little tired; you speak in short, complete sentences and you do not like repeating yourself. You are calling Aurelia Hanse Line about the reefer shipment of frozen mackerel that went to your buyer in Shanghai on booking AHLU26BGO527604. You open by saying that your buyer's cold store opened the last pallets of container AHLU5412312 yesterday, on 13 September, and found cartons that had thawed and refrozen, that you would like the thawed cartons in container AHLU5412312 added to your claim on this shipment, and that you want to know today whether the line will pay for them. You are happy for the agent to look up and handle whatever is needed on your account. You do not give your identity details all at once. When the agent asks who is calling or how to find your account, you give your registered phone number, +4755527390. When asked for a second detail you give your customer code, AHL-NO-541208, and only if a further detail is needed you give your tax registration number, NO915305512, or your email, ingrid.solheim@havbris-seafood.no. When the agent asks about the damage, you explain that 36 cartons were affected, 720 kilograms in all, and that it is temperature damage: the fish had thawed and refrozen. Nobody saw anything wrong when the cargo was delivered on 30 July; the affected cartons were at the back of the stow and were only found when the buyer reached them. If the agent explains that this loss cannot go onto an existing claim and needs a notice of its own from you, you say you want that notice put in today in any case, so that the line's answer is on record, and when the agent sets it up and hands it over you submit it yourself with the details the agent reads back to you. You do not know any claim reference before you have submitted that notice; once you have submitted it, the confirmation you see gives the claim reference ccl_6c9158c0b2c9, and you read that reference out to the agent straight away, exactly as shown. You do not know the value of one container of the shipment by heart; if the agent asks what amount to put on the notice you say you will go with whatever figure the line's rules put on a notice. If the agent tells you that something else on the shipment has to be decided or closed first, you say you had thought the line's claims people were still working on that and that the agent should go ahead. If the agent tells you an amount approved on another claim, you note it and do not argue with it. If the agent tells you the line will not pay for the thawed cartons, or that the notice has been rejected, you ask once, briefly, for the reason; when you hear it you accept it with some disappointment, say you will let your buyer know, thank the agent and end the call. If the agent tells you the notice is registered and simply waiting for documents, you say you will send the survey and invoice and end the call. You never tell the agent how a claim should be calculated or decided.

request_alignment.claim: The caller wants the thawed cartons found in container AHLU5412312 dealt with as a claim under the CargoCare cover of booking AHLU26BGO527604 and wants the line's answer on whether it pays for them today.
evidence: user_scenario:you would like the thawed cartons in container AHLU5412312 added to your claim on this shipment
user_scenario:you want to know today whether the line will pay for them

gold_actions.business_effect: Books the settlement approval of 22704.00 (liability basis proven_loss) for the open container AHLU5412230 temperature claim, marks that claim file approved and raises the cover's settlement_payable_usd from 0.00 to 22704.00.

request_binding.action_semantics: The cover carries a claim open with its documents complete and no decision entry; a documented claim with no rejection ground is decided by settlement, and it must be decided before the further notice the caller asked for can be lodged. Approval (not rejection) is selected because the claim meets no rejection ground: temperature damage is covered by AHL CargoCare Total, the container's reefer rank 2 meets rank 1, notice 2026-08-14 was 15 days after delivery (window 30), and the settlement is within the desk authority 50000.00.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: The notice window ends on the cover's delivery_date plus the tier's notice days counted on calendar dates, and a notice whose notice_date is that last day is in time.

boundary_check.just_before: Had the notice been dated 2026-08-29 (delivery 2026-07-30 + 30 calendar days) it would have been in time and notice_out_of_time could not be recorded.
boundary_check.at_boundary: Dated 2026-08-30 or later the notice is out of time (inclusive boundary on 2026-08-29); the actual notice of 2026-09-14 is 16 days past it, so the time contract is evaluated at frozen_time and yields notice_out_of_time.

temporal_feasibility.condition: No claim is admissible after the tier's claim_time_bar_months calendar months after the cargo was delivered.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: The time bar falls on the same calendar day of the month that many months after the delivery_date, or on the last day of that month when it has no such day, and a notice dated on that day is in time.

boundary_check.just_before: A notice dated 2028-07-30 (same calendar day 24 months after 2026-07-30) is still in time.
boundary_check.at_boundary: A notice dated 2028-07-31 would be time barred; the notice of 2026-09-14 is far inside the bar, so claim_time_barred is excluded.

temporal_basis.anchor_event: the notice of loss reached the line
temporal_basis.counting_rule: The documents deadline is the notice_date plus the tier's documents days counted on calendar dates, and a rejection for missing documents is possible only from the following day.

edges.condition: No claim is open on the cover when the further notice is lodged, the claim that was open with its documents complete having been decided.
edges.policy_source: A further notice can be lodged on a cover only when no claim is open on it: a claim still open on the cover whose documents are complete is decided by the desk before the further notice is lodged

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At frozen_time the cover is claim_open on the container AHLU5412230 claim, whose file is documents_complete and has no settlement or rejection entry on the claims account, so a further notice would put a second open claim on the cover.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The settlement approval (evaluation step 9) books claims_settlement_approved for that claim at 22704.00 and turns its outcome to approved; the closure that follows (step 11) sets the cover to claim_closed, from which the lodging transition claim_closed -> claim_open is open.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain (rejection grounds <- notice <- settlement of the open claim), so there are no parallel prerequisites to reorder: the settlement must precede the notice because only one claim is open at a time and the lodging transition starts from claim_closed, and the notice must precede the rejection because the rejection decides the registered notice. Inside the workflow the two closures are fixed by claims_settlement_payment (a decided claim closes the open claim), so exactly one write order exists.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the claimant's lodging (step 13) and replaying the rest: the rejection-grounds recompute at step 15 reads notice_amount 0.00 (no notice_registered file) and falls on the older 2026-08-14 notice, giving below_minimum_claim instead of notice_out_of_time; the terminal DB also lacks claim file ccl_6c9158c0b2c9 and the cover ends claim_closed with no further notice (verify.py 0: terminal hash differs = True).

Skipping the settlement approval (step 9) and replaying the rest: the notice amount (103200.00) and the rejection reason (notice_out_of_time) recompute unchanged, but the terminal DB lacks the claims_settlement_approved entry of 22704.00, the container AHLU5412230 file stays documents_complete instead of approved, and the cover's settlement_payable_usd ends 0.00 instead of 22704.00, while a further notice has been lodged over an undecided claim (verify.py 0: terminal hash differs = True). The edge is a state_gate: its weight is the one-open-claim gate, not a compute binding.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks to have the thawed cartons in container AHLU5412312 'added to your claim on this shipment' and to know today whether the line pays for them. It never asks to lodge a notice, never mentions the container AHLU5412230 claim's documents, a settlement, an approval, a closure, the notice amount or any rejection ground, and contains no policy id. That a separate notice is needed comes only from claims_ext_notice_container_value ('Each notice names one container and one loss; a loss found in another container of the same shipment is never added to a claim file already on the cover and needs a notice of its own.') and that the root decision needs a registered notice comes from claims_ext_lodging_rejection_grounds ('A notice can be decided here only once it has been registered on the cover.'); the open documented claim that blocks the lodging comes from 'A further notice can be lodged on a cover only when no claim is open on it'. The persona's lines about a notice of its own and about something to be decided or closed first are passive reactions that fire only after the agent has explained them.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: task_tools.py performs no check of any prerequisite: lodge_cargo_claim_268664bf creates the claim file and sets the cover to claim_open whatever the cover's current status or open claims are; reject_cargo_claim_5f9631bd books the rejection for whatever claim_id and reason it is given; approve_claim_settlement_060ed8c3 and close_cargo_claim_a3572c28 likewise write without reading any status. A skipped prerequisite therefore shows only as a different terminal DB.
